newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia dlr breaks higher as wages cut rate risk.
newsitem.headline: Australia dlr breaks higher as wages cut rate risk.

text.p: The Australian dollar leapt 1/4 cent to clear tough US$0.7830 resistance at the midsession after strong wages data seemed to put paid to the risk of a rate cut, at least in the short term.

The closely watched measure on average weekly ordinary time earnings jumped 1.3 percent in Q1 against forecasts of a 0.8 percent gain. Annual growth surged to 4.6 percent from 3.9 percent in Q4, putting it within the Reserve Bank's danger zone of 4.5-5.0 percent.
Money market rates shot up on the news and dealers saw scope for a rally to US$0.7860 and even US$0.7895 near term.
By 12.15 pm (0215 GMT) the dollar had leapt to US$0.7837/42 from an early US$0.7808/13 and US$0.7813/18 late here Wednesday.

Traders said it was meeting offers atop US$0.7840 amid much talk of big sell orders lurking in the wings, partly from a local bank which took out a truck load of call options last week related to the purchase of a Victorian state power station.

"It might take a while to soak this selling up, but so far the bids are coming strong and fast and look like winning out in the end," said one at a local bank. "Yield spreads have really swung in the Aussie's favour this week and it's attracting a lot of offshore demand, especially from Japan."

The revival in Japanese demand had been confirmed Wednesday with the launch of two yen/A$ dual currency samurai bonds worth a total 55 billion yen and another 10 billion yen reverse samurai had come this morning.

There was talk of more in the pipeline and the A$ responded by climbing to 99.56/66 yen from 99.15/25 late Wednesday, close to the five year high around 99.80 set in early April. In trade weighted terms it shot to 61.0 from a previous 60.7 close.
This was a complete turnaround for the currency which had been fast losing its appeal as yield spreads over the U.S. grew steadily narrower in recent weeks.

Expectations of another U.S. hike by the Federal Reserve and the lingering chance of an easing here had seen spreads on one and two year bonds tuern negative and forward rates for one year dollars swing to their highest premium in more than a decade.

Things had changed this week as a subdued set of U.S. employment cost data had seen Treasury prices rally sharply, while today's shocker on domestic wages had sent Australian rates climbing across the curve.
The surprise at the jump in earnings was all the greater as the market had thought wage pressure was waning after a moderate national minimum wage settlement last week.
In fact the 1.3 percent rise in AWOTE was the biggest gain since Q2 1995 and topped even the highest market forecast.

There were signs of strength outside the full-time adult sector as well since total earnings for all employees, including part-time, leapt 1.7 percent in the qaurter taking annual growth to 3.8 percent from just 2.8 percent in Q4.

Analysts cautioned the strength may have been concentrated in the state sector making the inlfationary implications less than otherwise, but the breakdown between private and public would not be released until May 22. Nevertheless it still made it hard for ther RBA to ease at its board meeting next week.

"But at this point in time you'd have to say that certainly a number like 4.6 percent is too high to be comfortable for the Reserve Bank," said Rob Henderon, chief economist at Dresdner Australia. "So basically forget any prospect of another cut in interest rates until it becomes clear that this is not a sign of accelerating wages growth."

The AWOTE completely overshadowed a soft 1.8 percent fall in building approvals for March which confounded forecasts of a 2.0 percent gain. All the weakness was in the volatile non-house sector and private sector housing rose 4.1 percent.
